title: The crate that won't budge
hook: You push a heavy crate and nothing moves. How hard is friction pushing back?

knows: forces in newtons; balanced forces mean no change in motion
doesNotKnow: that static friction adjusts to match the push, up to a limit mu_s N
that the limit is a ceiling, not the friction that always acts

misconception: Friction is always a fixed amount, mu N, even when the object is not sliding.
objective: The learner can explain that a crate that stays still feels friction exactly equal to the push (50 N for a 50 N push), up to the grip limit mu_s m g = 98.1 N, beyond which it slips.

claims.text: While the crate does not move, the friction on it exactly equals your push.
claims.source: Newton's first law: an object at rest has zero net force, so the horizontal static friction equals the applied push in size and opposes it.

claims.text: Static friction can grow only up to a limit, μs × N; for a 20 kg crate with μs = 0.50 on a level floor that is 0.50 × 20 × 9.81 = 98.1 N.
claims.source: Static friction f_s <= mu_s N (OpenStax University Physics Vol. 1, section 6.2 Friction); N = m g on a level floor; 0.5 x 20 x 9.81 = 98.10 N (artifacts/scratch/w4phys/check.mjs).

claims.text: A push above the grip limit makes the crate slip; once it slides, a different (sliding) friction acts, which this lesson does not model.
claims.source: Kinetic friction f_k = mu_k N with mu_k usually below mu_s (OpenStax University Physics Vol. 1, section 6.2). The stage shows 'slips!' and 'sliding' with no friction number.

claims.text: μs = 0.50 is an illustrative value; real crates and floors vary.
claims.source: Stated on stage ('illustrative') and in the reveal. Tabulated static coefficients for wood on wood or concrete range roughly 0.25-0.6 (e.g. Engineering ToolBox, Friction and Friction Coefficients table), so 0.50 is plausible but not measured for any particular crate.

recall.question: A box can grip the floor with at most 200 N of friction. You push it with 30 N and it stays still. How big is the friction on it?
recall.why: A box at rest has no net force, so friction exactly cancels the 30 N push. The 200 N is only the most friction can give before the box slips.
